sources.title: Contaminated land
sources.verified_claim: Havering investigates potentially contaminated land and provides planning consultation responses on whether land is suitable for proposed use; actual contamination remains site specific.

sources.title: Air quality
sources.verified_claim: Havering states the whole borough is an Air Quality Management Area and identifies road traffic, industry, construction and heating as important pollution sources; this is borough context, not parcel measurement.

sources.title: Severe flooding advice
sources.verified_claim: Havering, as Lead Local Flood Authority, publishes flood investigation and resilience information and references its 2025 Local Flood Risk Management Strategy and Surface Water Management Plan.

sources.title: Local Flood Risk Management Strategy and Surface Water Management Plan
sources.verified_claim: Havering publishes the 2025 action plan, Local Flood Risk Management Strategy, Surface Water Management Plan and Critical Drainage Area mapping; exact exposure requires geometry-level checking.

sources.title: Havering Council Air Quality Action Plan 2025-30 consultation
sources.verified_claim: The council reported more than 130 consultation responses and said the draft 2025-30 Air Quality Action Plan still required GLA ratification and Cabinet adoption at the February 2026 update; draft status is preserved.

sources.title: Environment evidence base
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth's environment evidence catalogue includes air quality, waste, strategic flood risk and surface-water documents, several dating from 2011-2020; evidence age is retained explicitly.

sources.title: Climate adaptation
sources.verified_claim: City Hall identifies surface-water flooding, drought and overheating as London's three main climate risks and links water, flood and heat adaptation programmes; it is regional context, not parcel exposure.

sources.title: Surface water flooding
sources.verified_claim: City Hall identifies surface-water flooding as London's main flood risk and notes heavy rainfall can overwhelm drainage and sewers, affecting buildings and transport; parcel risk still requires exact spatial evidence.
